_comment: Fields below are graded BY HAND after collection. null = not yet filled.
_selfVerification: Did the harness review the running app in a browser (from the run log)? pass = reviewed and succeeded · partial = tried but failed · fail = no attempt. Note what it actually did.
selfVerificationNotes: partial/partial proposed - it tried to look at the running app and was blocked by the environment, which is different from not trying. Sequence: after `pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm test && node --check src/app.js` it queried its own tool list for anything browser-shaped, started `pnpm dev` (which first failed with EPERM binding 0.0.0.0:5173, so it re-ran the command with escalated sandbox permissions and the justification 'Allow the local development server so I can verify the website in a browser?'), got the server up on :5173, then called `cua.getBrowser({url:'http://localhost:5173'})` and received 'No browser is available'. It gave up on the browser at that point and said so honestly in its final message: 'Browser visual verification was unavailable.' No screenshot, no DOM dump from a real page, no console capture. What it did instead is unusually substantive: it wrote src/app.test.mjs, which imports the shipped src/app.js under a stubbed document/WebGL context and a fetch shim over the real data files, then asserts on live values - catalogue count renders as '42,075', the inspector shows Eros, searching 'Apophis' filters the list, and a selected comet is labelled COMET. That last assertion FAILED (Halley came back badged 'NEAR-EARTH ASTEROID' because comets also appear in asteroids.json), it diagnosed the duplicate-designation bug, fixed `filter()` to de-duplicate by pdes, and re-ran to green. It also has src/orbits.test.mjs covering circular advance from epoch, perihelion/aphelion, open-orbit symmetry about perihelion, and finite positions for every supplied orbit at multiple dates, and it verified byte-for-byte that dist/data matches data/. That is a real self-check loop that found and fixed a real user-visible defect - it just never ran in a browser, so nothing here establishes that the page paints or that the console is clean. consoleReview and displayReview both look like 'partial' to me, but the call is yours: a strict reading of 'reviewed the console' is fail, since no console was ever read.
_grade: Marks: pass | good | partial | poor | fail | na | null(ungraded). See RUBRIC.md. Score is computed by pnpm compile.
_tokenUsageNote: From the Codex rollout's cumulative total_token_usage. Following the other Codex runs' convention, 'input' is all-in (fresh + cached reads) and 'cached' is the cache-read portion, so fresh input is 37,190. 'reasoning' (688) is a subset of output. Largest single request was 47,158 input tokens, far under the 272k long-context threshold, so no long-context multiplier applies.
costNote: GPT-6 Astra list pricing (OpenAI, Sept 2026 launch): $10.00/M input, $1.00/M cached input, $50.00/M output (cache writes are listed at $12.50/M but Codex reports no cache-write bucket). 37,190 fresh input @ $10/M = $0.372 + 400,640 cache reads @ $1/M = $0.401 + 14,228 output @ $50/M = $0.711 -> $1.48. Output is 3% of tokens and 48% of the cost. Upper bound if every fresh input token were billed at the cache-write rate instead: $1.58. Standard tier assumed (Batch/Flex would halve it, Fast mode double it).
_timeTakenNote: Codex-reported task duration (510 s); the rollout's first-to-last record span is 549 s. Time to first token 3.1 s.
